visible.summary:
Risaralda carries no local statute aimed at trans people and no department-level incident entry in the audited record; what a trans visitor stands under is Colombia's national pattern. That pattern is violent and largely unpunished: armed groups circulated "social cleansing" flyers naming trans women as targets in 2024, at least 41 trans women were killed nationally in 2023 and 13 more in the first quarter of 2025, and of 155 criminal investigations into LGBTQ killings only 3 reached a verdict last year — roughly 2% against a 9% overall homicide-conviction rate.

State response to this violence is episodic rather than structural: the audited record shows a presidential order to investigate after a viral April 2025 murder of a trans woman in another department, vigils, and nothing resembling standing local protection machinery. Outside the largest cities the national figures are the operative risk for a visitor here.
